problem_statement: `epic-harness --version` (also `-v` and the `version` subcommand) writes the version string to stderr, so `$(epic-harness --version)` captures nothing in scripts. The version must go to stdout with an empty stderr and exit code 0, for all three forms.

`epic evolve accept-synth` hangs forever when run headless: when stdin is not a TTY it reads the body until EOF, and callers such as an agent's Bash tool keep stdin open without ever closing it. The hook subcommands already avoid this hang; `accept-synth` must too. When no body arrives in time and no `--stdin` flag was given, it should exit promptly with its usage error instead of hanging.

Hook subcommands (`resume`, `guard`, `polish`, `observe`, `snapshot`, `reflect`) hang forever when invoked headless. When stdin is not a TTY they read the hook payload until EOF, but some callers (for example the Claude Code Bash tool) hold stdin open as a socket that never reaches EOF. Observed: `epic-harness reflect` sat at 0% CPU for 15+ minutes inside an orbit run. Hosts that pipe a payload and close stdin must still receive the full payload, but a caller that never closes stdin must not block the command: it should proceed with empty input after a short bound (a few seconds) and exit normally.

The Grok plugin manifest `.grok-plugin/hooks.json` still uses POSIX inline shell handlers, while the Codex manifest already routes every handler through the shell-free launcher. The inline form swallows guard's exit code on Grok. Migrate the Grok manifest to the same contract as Codex: every handler command is exactly `node ${GROK_PLUGIN_ROOT}/registry/scripts/hooks/run.mjs <subcommand>` with no shell syntax. Grok must keep `guard` registered for PreToolUse `Bash` (and must not run `observe` there), `observe` on PostToolUse `*`, `resume` on SessionStart `*`, and `snapshot` on PreCompact, matching the other hosts.
test_cmd: cargo test --no-fail-fast -- all_hosts_snapshot_before_compaction assert_launcher_form codex_hook_commands_all_use_launcher grok_hook_commands_all_use_launcher grok_registers_guard_observe_and_resume

problem_statement: Resuming a session can restore another project's snapshot. `get_latest_snapshot_pool(pool, project)` returns the newest row by id among the project's own snapshots and legacy rows with an empty project, so a legacy unattributed row with a higher id shadows the project's own latest snapshot. A project's own snapshots must win over legacy unattributed rows; a project with no snapshots of its own must still fall back to the legacy unattributed history.
gold_patch:
diff --git a/src/store/sessions.rs b/src/store/sessions.rs
index aad4c7a..f5df542 100644
--- a/src/store/sessions.rs
+++ b/src/store/sessions.rs
@@ -50,17 +50,22 @@ pub async fn insert_snapshot_pool(
 /// Get the most recent session snapshot for `project`.
 ///
 /// Rows written before snapshots were attributed carry an empty project and
-/// stay visible to every project — dropping them would silently discard the
-/// existing history on upgrade.
+/// stay visible as a fallback — dropping them would silently discard the
+/// existing history on upgrade. They are ordered *after* this project's own
+/// rows: under a plain `ORDER BY id DESC`, a leftover unattributed row from
+/// another project with a higher id would win and resume this project into a
+/// foreign session.
 pub async fn get_latest_snapshot_pool(
     pool: &AnyPool,
     project: &str,
 ) -> io::Result<Option<SessionSnapshot>> {
     let row = sqlx::query(
         "SELECT timestamp, snap_type, summary, pending_tasks, context_usage, pipeline_state
-         FROM sessions WHERE project = ? OR project = '' ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1",
+         FROM sessions WHERE project = ? OR project = ''
+         ORDER BY CASE WHEN project = ? THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, id DESC LIMIT 1",
     )
     .bind(project)
+    .bind(project)
     .fetch_optional(pool)
     .await
     .map_err(super::sqlx_err)?;

problem_statement: The observe hook treats `sed -i ...` (in-place edit, including `-i.bak` and `--in-place`) as a read-only command. Read-only commands are exempt from failure detection on merged stdout/stderr output, so a failing in-place sed is never counted as a failure. In-place sed modifies files and must not be classified as read-only; plain `sed -n ...` reads stay read-only.

`is_read_only_command` misclassifies pipelines. It looks at the command as a whole, so a pure-read pipeline such as `rg foo | head` is not recognized as read-only (and gets scanned for failure keywords), while a pipeline that ends in a writing stage (for example `cat x | tee out` or `... | sed -i ...`) can be treated as read-only. A pipeline is read-only only when every stage is read-only.

On Claude Code, spawned subagents never show as Running in the live-agent view; every agent goes straight to Done. The orchestrator tracks a spawn when `epic observe` receives a PreToolUse event for the `Agent` tool, but `.claude-plugin/hooks.json` registers PreToolUse only for `Bash`, so that event never reaches `observe`. Fix the Claude manifest so `epic observe` runs on PreToolUse for `Agent`, while guard stays scoped to `Bash`.

problem_statement: The MCP bridge's `list_sessions` output shows an 8-character id prefix per session. Codex session ids are UUIDv7, whose first 8 hex characters encode a second-resolution timestamp, so sessions started in the same second render with identical prefixes (one listing showed 22 rows with the same visible id). The rendered prefix must be long enough to tell such sessions apart, and the displayed prefix must still work as a lookup key for `read_session`.

The guard's secret redaction can corrupt JSON request bodies. When a detected span ends on a backslash that starts a JSON escape pair (for example `\"`), splicing the span out leaves a stray quote and the body no longer parses (upstream answers 422 json_invalid). Redaction must never split a JSON escape pair, and a redacted body must remain valid JSON.

`claudy handoff` misses or misorders recent agy sessions. It ranks sessions by `last_modified_time` from agy's `conversation_summaries.db`, but that index goes stale: a live session can carry an old summary time while its conversation file on disk is fresh. Session ranking must reflect the conversation file's modification time when the file exists, so a live session with a stale summary ranks above an idle session with a newer summary time.

problem_statement: AgentGlance ignores Grok hook events. Grok sends snake_case event names on stdin (`user_prompt_submit`, `stop`, `notification`) instead of the PascalCase names other hosts use, so the hook exits 0 without updating the SmallTV display. Map them to the same display states as their PascalCase equivalents (`UserPromptSubmit` = working, `Stop` = done, `Notification` = waiting), including when the event name arrives through the environment-variable fallback. Existing PascalCase handling must keep working.

+"""Grok sends snake_case event values; Claude/Codex send PascalCase.
+
+A UserPromptSubmit hook that ignores `user_prompt_submit` looks successful

+import importlib.util
+import os
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+
+
+def load_script():
+    path = ROOT / "scripts" / "agent_glance.py"
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("agent_glance", path)
+    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
+    return mod
+
+
+class EventMapTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        cls.ag = load_script()
+
+    def _state(self, payload, env=None):
+        saved = {}
+        if env:
+            for k, v in env.items():
+                saved[k] = os.environ.get(k)
+                if v is None:
+                    os.environ.pop(k, None)
+                else:
+                    os.environ[k] = v
+        try:
+            ev, _tp = self.ag._norm_event(payload)
+            return self.ag._resolve_state_key(ev, payload), ev
+        finally:
+            for k, old in saved.items():
+                if old is None:
+                    os.environ.pop(k, None)
+                else:
+                    os.environ[k] = old
+
+    def test_grok_user_prompt_submit_is_working(self):
+        state, ev = self._state({"hookEventName": "user_prompt_submit"})
+        self.assertEqual(ev, "UserPromptSubmit")
+        self.assertEqual(state, "working")
+
+    def test_grok_stop_is_done(self):
+        state, ev = self._state({"hookEventName": "stop"})
+        self.assertEqual(ev, "Stop")
+        self.assertEqual(state, "done")
+
+    def test_grok_notification_is_waiting(self):
+        state, ev = self._state({"hookEventName": "notification"})
+        self.assertEqual(ev, "Notification")
+        self.assertEqual(state, "waiting")
+
+    def test_claude_pascal_case_still_works(self):
+        state, ev = self._state({"hook_event_name": "UserPromptSubmit"})
+        self.assertEqual(ev, "UserPromptSubmit")
+        self.assertEqual(state, "working")
+
+    def test_grok_hook_event_env_fallback(self):
+        state, ev = self._state({}, env={"GROK_HOOK_EVENT": "user_prompt_submit"})
+        self.assertEqual(ev, "UserPromptSubmit")
+        self.assertEqual(state, "working")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

problem_statement: The read hook (`registry/scripts/read-hook.mjs`) only finds the file path for Claude Code and Codex payloads (`tool_input.file_path`). Grok sends the path as `target_file` and agy sends it as `AbsolutePath`, so on those hosts the hook never transpiles the document. `extractFilePath` must also handle those payload shapes.

Anthropic streaming responses always report `prompt_tokens` and `total_tokens` of 0. Input usage arrives in `message_start` (`message.usage`: `input_tokens`, `cache_creation_input_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens`) and later `message_delta` events may carry cumulative input fields, but the client only reads output tokens from `message_delta`. Streaming usage must count input tokens including both cache token kinds, treat missing usage fields as 0, and fill prompt and total tokens from `message_delta` when it carries cumulative input fields.

DLP redaction can corrupt JSON bodies (seen as upstream 422 errors through claudy --guard). The `key_value_assignment` rule's value pattern consumes backslashes one at a time, so a detected span can end on the first byte of a JSON escape like `\"`; splicing the span out leaves a bare quote. Spans must never end in the middle of an escape pair, and values that contain raw backslashes which are not escapes must still be detected.
